summary: The bill amends the Natural Gas Act to require the Secretary of Energy to conduct climate, economic, and environmental justice assessments and approve a natural gas export application only upon finding it will not significantly worsen climate change, raise U.S. consumer energy prices, or burden vulnerable communities.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends regulatory procedures for LNG export approvals under the Natural Gas Act and NEPA but contains no provisions altering federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgets.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration policy or border enforcement.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense budgets or policy.

The bill's core purpose is to require the Department of Energy to assess and deny LNG export permits if they would significantly contribute to climate change, increase GHG emissions across the full lifecycle, hinder the global energy transition, or impose disproportionate environmental burdens on vulnerable communities. It mandates use of 20-year GWP for methane, social cost of carbon calculations, and consistency with net-zero pathways by 2050. This directly expands environmental and climate protections.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions relate to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.

The bill eliminates the prior automatic public-interest approval for LNG exports to FTA countries and subjects all exports to a new climate/economic/environmental justice review process with a one-year deadline. This adds regulatory hurdles to energy exports but is framed entirely around domestic climate and consumer protections rather than traditional trade or tariff policy.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions relate to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access or election procedures.
No provisions relate to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill requires assessments of impacts on fisheries employment and low-income/working families but does not address union rights, collective bargaining, or labor law.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
